To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best model for retrieving the next sentence of a story is the one that selects the sentence that is most similar to the previous sentence of the story, and that this similarity can be calculated by comparing the words that are in the previous sentence but are not in the story so far.
the best story is generated when we use a retrieval model that combines a measure of semantic relatedness with a measure of sentence similarity.

(a) retrieval models are more important for story generation than for summarization, (b) a model based on a single latent topic vector is the best retrieval model for open domain story generation, (c) the best model for open domain summarization is a combination of a single latent topic and a latent document vector, and (d) for open domain summarizations the best retrieval model is a single latent document vector.

the best retrieval models for open domain story generation are the ones that are most faithful to the original story corpus.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the most effective retrieval model for story continuation depends on the specific task and user population, and that the best model may be a hybrid of several models.

the most effective retrieval model for story generation is a combination of the most similar sentence to the current story and the most similar sentence in the story so far, with a small penalty for sentences that have already been used in the story.
a simple retrieval model based on the cosine similarity of sentence embeddings outperforms the other models in terms of story coherence and overall user ratings.
